key_insight: Symbolic regression discovers a compact, interpretable skin-friction law for attached flows that extends classical flat-plate theory using pressure and Mach-number corrections.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, low-cost skin-friction and drag estimation for airfoils across subsonic to supersonic regimes without running expensive viscous CFD every time.
method: Use limited paired data from Euler surface solutions and viscous-flow skin-friction coefficients.
Apply symbolic regression to build a progressive analytical formula chain.
Add correction terms for surface pressure variation and Mach-number effects to preserve physical interpretability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on typical geometries with low average integrated skin-friction drag prediction error and good generalization across freestream conditions and shapes.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the training data, especially for flow regimes or geometries outside the attached-flow regime used in discovery.
paper_title: Skin friction prediction for attached flows based on two-dimensional inviscid solutions
